description: Quality telemetry: refinement attempts from ClickHouse, writer health from Prometheus. Empty panels in production are expected until SSF_QUALITY_TELEMETRY_MODE is set to `enabled`. Feedback KPIs (#304) read the silver tier for exact averages and the gold tier for history; the gold averages are approximate under re-emission and say so.

panels.title: Conversation Completion Rate
panels.description: KPI U2. Sessions activated in the time range that carried at least one successful message in each direction, divided by all sessions activated in the range. 'Successful' is the gateway pipeline outcome, not a recipient acknowledgement, and the event does not record whether both parties were connected. Sessions activated shortly before the end of the range may still be talking and read as incomplete, so a range ending now reads low. Follows the tenant picker.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * countIf(to_customer > 0 AND to_admin > 0) / nullIf(count(), 0), 1) AS completion_rate FROM (SELECT session_ref, countIf(event_type = 'session_lifecycle' AND lifecycle_phase = 'activated') AS activated, countIf(event_type = 'translation_message' AND terminal_outcome = 'success' AND direction = 'admin_to_customer') AS to_customer, countIf(event_type = 'translation_message' AND terminal_outcome = 'success' AND direction = 'customer_to_admin') AS to_admin FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type IN ('session_lifecycle', 'translation_message') AND match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) GROUP BY session_ref) WHERE activated > 0

panels.title: Delivery Success Rate
panels.description: KPI Q3, upper-bound proxy. Share of broadcasts that every registered socket and polling queue of the session accepted -- the ratio the WebSocketBroadcastFailureRateHigh alert watches. The sender's own socket counts, so a message sent while the recipient is offline still reads as delivered. A broadcast is undelivered only when nobody at all was registered or a send failed. There is no recipient acknowledgement and no expired state.

panels.title: Unexpected Disconnect Rate
panels.description: KPI R2. Disconnects with a reason other than a normal end, divided by connections opened in the range. 'Normal' is the same reason list the WebSocketConnectionFailures alert excludes. Each client_type and reason series is created by its first event in a gateway process, and increase() cannot see that event, so after every restart the first disconnect and the first connection per series go uncounted. Pre-initialising the label combinations in WebSocketMonitor._setup_prometheus_metrics would remove this bias and is worth doing.

panels.title: Heartbeat Timeouts per 1,000 Connection-Minutes
panels.description: KPI R4. Heartbeat-timeout disconnects per 1,000 minutes of connection time. Connection time is recorded when a connection closes: a connection still open at the end of the range is missing from the denominator (reads high), while a long connection closing inside the range brings all its minutes, including those before the range (reads low). The first heartbeat timeout per client_type after a gateway restart is not counted, because that event creates its series and increase() cannot see it. Pre-initialising the label combinations in WebSocketMonitor._setup_prometheus_metrics would remove this bias and is worth doing.

panels.title: Stage Success Rate
panels.description: KPIs A1, T1, S1, R6. A message reached a stage if the stage recorded a duration or the message failed there. Durations are whole milliseconds, so a stage that finishes in under 1 ms stores 0 and is not counted as reached. Failures with failed_stage unknown belong to no stage and are not counted; see Message Failures by Stage. Follows the tenant picker.

targets.rawSql: SELECT stage, countIf(duration > 0 OR failed_stage = stage) AS reached, countIf(failed_stage = stage) AS failed, round(100 * (reached - failed) / nullIf(reached, 0), 1) AS success_rate FROM quality_events FINAL ARRAY JOIN ['asr', 'translation', 'tts'] AS stage, [asr_duration_ms, translation_duration_ms, tts_duration_ms] AS duration WHERE event_type = 'translation_message' AND match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) GROUP BY stage ORDER BY indexOf(['asr', 'translation', 'tts'], stage)

panels.title: Message Latency by Input Mode
panels.description: KPI Q1, proxy. Time from the gateway accepting a successful message until it has stored it and sent it to the session's sockets and polling queues, split into text and audio. It does not wait for the recipient to acknowledge delivery, which no event records yet. Follows the tenant picker.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfInterval(emitted_at_utc, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time, input_mode, quantile(0.5)(total_duration_ms) AS p50, quantile(0.95)(total_duration_ms) AS p95, max(total_duration_ms) AS max FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'translation_message' AND terminal_outcome = 'success' AND match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) GROUP BY time, input_mode ORDER BY time

panels.title: Ratings of 4 or 5
panels.description: KPIs F2/SQ1, F7/SQ2, F3/SQ3. Share of submissions rating 4 or 5 on each 1-5 question, filtered by tenant. The form asks about translation quality, performance and usability -- close to, not worded as, the catalogue's SQ1-SQ3. Silver keeps 30 days.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * countIf(translation_quality >= 4) / nullIf(count(), 0), 1) AS translation_quality, round(100 * countIf(performance >= 4) / nullIf(count(), 0), 1) AS performance, round(100 * countIf(usability >= 4) / nullIf(count(), 0), 1) AS usability FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'feedback_submitted' AND match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)

panels.title: Pipeline Queue Wait p95
panels.description: KPI R9. Time a request waited for an admission slot, admitted or rejected.

panels.title: Pipeline In-Flight and Rejections
panels.description: KPI R9. Any sustained rejection rate means users are seeing SYSTEM_BUSY.

panels.title: Refinement Outcomes
panels.description: Refinement attempts per outcome, counted with increase() over each interval rather than rate(): production sees only a handful of refinements a day, a rate too low for rate() to render as anything but a flat zero line (the same reasoning behind RefinementFailureRateHigh using increase()). This is the metric alerting reads; the ClickHouse-backed Outcome Mix panel below is dashboard-only and does not page anyone.

panels.title: Refinement Requests In Flight
panels.description: vLLM's own request queue depth. Metric name is documented but unverified against a running server; the server is stood up in a later task, which must confirm the name before relying on this panel.

panels.title: KV Cache Utilisation
panels.description: vLLM's KV cache occupancy. Metric name is documented but unverified against a running server; the server is stood up in a later task, which must confirm the name before relying on this panel.

targets.rawSql: SELECT count() AS sessions FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'session_lifecycle' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) AND lifecycle_phase = 'created'
SELECT count() AS sessions FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'session_lifecycle' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) AND lifecycle_phase = 'activated'
SELECT quantile(0.5)(session_duration_ms) AS p50 FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'session_lifecycle' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) AND lifecycle_phase = 'terminated'
SELECT avg(message_count) AS messages FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'session_lifecycle' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) AND lifecycle_phase = 'terminated'

SELECT toStartOfInterval(emitted_at_utc, INTERVAL 1 HOUR) AS time, lifecycle_phase, count() AS sessions FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'session_lifecycle' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) GROUP BY time, lifecycle_phase ORDER BY time

SELECT termination_reason, count() AS sessions, round(avg(message_count), 1) AS avg_messages FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'session_lifecycle' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) AND lifecycle_phase = 'terminated' GROUP BY termination_reason ORDER BY sessions DESC
SELECT countIf(message_count = 0) AS empty_sessions FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'session_lifecycle' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) AND lifecycle_phase = 'terminated'
SELECT count() AS messages FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'translation_message' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)
SELECT 100 * countIf(terminal_outcome = 'success') / count() AS success_rate FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'translation_message' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)
SELECT quantile(0.95)(total_duration_ms) AS p95 FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'translation_message' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)
SELECT countIf(terminal_outcome = 'failure') AS failures FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'translation_message' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)

SELECT toStartOfInterval(emitted_at_utc, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time, quantile(0.5)(total_duration_ms) AS p50, quantile(0.95)(total_duration_ms) AS p95, quantile(0.99)(total_duration_ms) AS p99 FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'translation_message' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

SELECT toStartOfInterval(emitted_at_utc, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time, quantile(0.95)(nullIf(asr_duration_ms, 0)) AS asr, quantile(0.95)(nullIf(translation_duration_ms, 0)) AS translation, quantile(0.95)(nullIf(refinement_duration_ms, 0)) AS refinement, quantile(0.95)(nullIf(tts_duration_ms, 0)) AS tts FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'translation_message' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

SELECT failed_stage, error_code, count() AS messages FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'translation_message' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) AND terminal_outcome = 'failure' GROUP BY failed_stage, error_code ORDER BY messages DESC

SELECT toStartOfInterval(emitted_at_utc, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time, concat(direction, ' / ', input_mode) AS flow, count() AS messages FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'translation_message' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) GROUP BY time, flow ORDER BY time
SELECT count() AS attempts FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'refinement_attempt' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)

panels.title: Refinement Attempts
panels.description: Shadow candidate runs recorded in the selected range. Empty means the gateway is not in `enabled` mode, or the collector is not delivering.

targets.rawSql: SELECT quantile(0.95)(refinement_latency_ms) AS p95_ms FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'refinement_attempt' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)

panels.title: Candidate Latency p95
panels.description: The number the refinement benchmarking work needs and has never had: candidate latency was measured and thrown away into a log line.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * countIf(refinement_changed = 1) / greatest(count(), 1), 1) AS changed_pct FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'refinement_attempt' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)

panels.title: Text Changed
panels.description: Share of attempts where the candidate model actually altered the translation. A rate near zero means the model is earning nothing.

targets.rawSql: SELECT countIf(error_code NOT IN ('none', '')) AS failures FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'refinement_attempt' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)

panels.title: Failed Attempts
panels.description: Attempts that ended in a classified failure. The classification is a closed enum; the original message never leaves the gateway.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfInterval(emitted_at_utc, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time, quantile(0.5)(refinement_latency_ms) AS p50, quantile(0.95)(refinement_latency_ms) AS p95, quantile(0.99)(refinement_latency_ms) AS p99 FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'refinement_attempt' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

SELECT toStartOfInterval(emitted_at_utc, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time, model_ref, quantile(0.95)(refinement_latency_ms) AS p95_ms FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'refinement_attempt' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) AND model_ref != '' GROUP BY time, model_ref ORDER BY time

panels.title: Latency p95 by Model
panels.description: Model comparison. This is the question `add-phi-refinement-benchmarking` asks; a shadow deployment of a second model populates both series.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfInterval(emitted_at_utc, INTERVAL 5 MINUTE) AS time, refinement_outcome, count() AS attempts FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'refinement_attempt' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) AND refinement_outcome != '' GROUP BY time, refinement_outcome ORDER BY time

SELECT error_code, count() AS attempts FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'refinement_attempt' AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) AND error_code NOT IN ('none', '') GROUP BY error_code ORDER BY attempts DESC

panels.title: Failures by Error Code
panels.description: The stable error taxonomy. New values here mean the classifier gained a case, not that an upstream changed its wording.

panels.title: Writer Health by Outcome
panels.description: `dropped_disallowed` here is a code defect: the six places that must agree about a field have diverged and data is being lost silently.

panels.title: Events Lost Before The Collector
panels.description: The gateway counted these as queued into the SDK; the collector never received them. The OTel SDK's BatchLogRecordProcessor reports its overflow drops nowhere else, so this gap is the only measurement of them - and the evidence that decides whether task 2.1 is real work.

targets.rawSql: SELECT 'quality_events (30 day TTL)' AS tier, toString(min(emitted_at_utc)) AS oldest_row, dateDiff('day', min(emitted_at_utc), now()) AS age_days FROM quality_events FINAL UNION ALL SELECT 'quality_events_daily (13 month TTL)' AS tier, toString(min(event_date)) AS oldest_row, dateDiff('day', toDateTime(min(event_date)), now()) AS age_days FROM quality_events_daily

panels.title: Retention Verification
panels.description: age_days above the tier's TTL means expiry is not running. ClickHouse fixes TTL at table creation, so a tier created without one can never be given one - check SHOW CREATE TABLE, not this panel alone.

targets.rawSql: SELECT event_date AS time, model_ref, uniqExactMerge(events) AS attempts FROM quality_events_daily WHERE event_type = 'refinement_attempt' AND model_ref != '' AND $__dateFilter(event_date) GROUP BY event_date, model_ref ORDER BY event_date

panels.title: Daily Attempts (Gold Tier)
panels.description: Read from the 13-month aggregate tier, not the 30-day raw tier. Counts are uniqExact over event_id so a retried delivery is not double-counted.

targets.rawSql: SELECT countIf(event_type = 'refinement_attempt' AND model_ref = '') + countIf(event_type = 'translation_message' AND session_ref = '') + countIf(event_type = 'session_lifecycle' AND lifecycle_phase = '') AS untyped FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)

panels.title: Rows Missing Typed Fields
panels.description: Should be zero. Anything else means refinement events were written while migration 002 was not yet applied, so the view projected only the envelope. Apply the migrations before switching the mode to `enabled`.

panels.title: Feedback Submissions
panels.description: Distinct submissions. uniqExact over event_id rather than count(), because #305 re-emits a failed delivery under the same id and the ReplacingMergeTree only collapses that duplicate at merge time.

targets.rawSql: SELECT uniqExact(event_id) AS submissions FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'feedback_submitted' AND match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)

panels.title: Feedback Response Rate
panels.description: Sessions that submitted feedback, over sessions that were activated. Submissions carrying no session reference are excluded from the numerator: the access-code and admin-dashboard screens submit without one, and every such row shares the same placeholder reference, so counting them would both collapse them into one session and let the rate exceed 100%.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * uniqExactIf(session_ref, event_type = 'feedback_submitted' AND session_ref != '00000000000000000000000000000000') / nullIf(uniqExactIf(session_ref, event_type = 'session_lifecycle' AND lifecycle_phase = 'activated'), 0), 1) AS response_rate FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)

panels.title: Net Promoter Score
panels.description: Promoters (9-10) minus detractors (0-6) as a percentage of submissions. Built on uniqExact, so it stays exact under re-emission -- unlike the gold tier's rating averages.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(100 * (uniqExactIf(event_id, net_promoter_score >= 9) - uniqExactIf(event_id, net_promoter_score <= 6)) / nullIf(uniqExact(event_id), 0)) AS nps FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'feedback_submitted' AND match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc)

panels.title: Submissions Awaiting Analytics
panels.description: Rows stored in PostgreSQL whose analytics event has not been delivered, as seen by the last reconciliation pass. The feedback itself is safe; only the ClickHouse half is behind, so the numbers on this row understate until it drains. Capped at the batch limit of 200.

panels.title: Rating Averages
panels.description: Exact: averaged over the deduplicated silver rows. Silver keeps 30 days, so a longer time range silently truncates here -- use the gold panel below for history, and read its caveat first.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfInterval(emitted_at_utc, INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS time, avg(translation_quality) AS translation_quality, avg(performance) AS performance, avg(usability) AS usability FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'feedback_submitted' AND match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Promoters, Passives and Detractors
panels.description: The split behind the score, so a moving NPS can be read as gaining promoters or losing detractors rather than as one number.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfInterval(emitted_at_utc, INTERVAL 1 DAY) AS time, uniqExactIf(event_id, net_promoter_score >= 9) AS promoters, uniqExactIf(event_id, net_promoter_score >= 7 AND net_promoter_score <= 8) AS passives, uniqExactIf(event_id, net_promoter_score <= 6) AS detractors FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'feedback_submitted' AND match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Daily Submissions (Gold Tier)
panels.description: Thirteen months of history, split by form version so a revised question set is visible rather than pooled. Exact: gold counts with uniqExact over event_id, so a re-emission does not inflate them. Filter by tenant with the Tenant picker. The breakdown starts when #325 shipped: rows aggregated before it carry no reference and sit under an empty tenant, which All includes and no single tenant does.

targets.rawSql: SELECT event_date AS time, feedback_form_version, uniqExactMerge(submissions) AS submissions FROM feedback_daily WHERE $__dateFilter(event_date) AND match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') GROUP BY event_date, feedback_form_version ORDER BY event_date

panels.title: Rating Averages (Gold Tier, approximate)
panels.description: APPROXIMATE BY CONSTRUCTION. avgState has no distinct-by form, so a submission re-emitted by the #305 reconciler contributes its ratings twice -- and #305 re-emits by design, not only after a fault. Verified against ClickHouse 26.3.17: two submissions of 9 and 3 read as an average of 7 after one retry, where the true value is 6. Counts and NPS on this dashboard are exact; these four averages are not. Inside 30 days, read 'Rating Averages'. Filter by tenant with the Tenant picker. The breakdown starts when #325 shipped: rows aggregated before it carry no reference and sit under an empty tenant, which All includes and no single tenant does.

targets.rawSql: SELECT event_date AS time, avgMerge(translation_quality_avg) AS translation_quality, avgMerge(performance_avg) AS performance, avgMerge(usability_avg) AS usability FROM feedback_daily WHERE $__dateFilter(event_date) AND match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') GROUP BY event_date ORDER BY event_date

panels.title: Ratings by Form Version
panels.description: The denominator beside the averages, which #304 asks for explicitly: an average of four submissions and an average of four hundred look identical without it.

targets.rawSql: SELECT feedback_form_version AS form_version, uniqExact(event_id) AS submissions, round(avg(translation_quality), 2) AS translation_quality, round(avg(performance), 2) AS performance, round(avg(usability), 2) AS usability, round(avg(net_promoter_score), 2) AS nps_mean FROM quality_events FINAL WHERE event_type = 'feedback_submitted' AND match(tenant_ref, '${tenant:regex}') AND $__timeFilter(emitted_at_utc) GROUP BY form_version ORDER BY submissions DESC

list.name: tenant
list.label: Tenant
list.description: Pseudonymous tenant reference, twelve hex characters. Every feedback panel honours it, in both tiers. So do the Go-live KPI panels that read ClickHouse. The older refinement, translation and session panels do not: they read quality_events_daily, which has no tenant dimension. References are fixed width, so the unanchored match() cannot select one tenant's rows into another's. Feedback aggregated before #325 carries no reference and appears only under All.
list.query: SELECT DISTINCT tenant_ref FROM feedback_daily WHERE tenant_ref NOT IN ('', '000000000000') ORDER BY tenant_ref

title: SSF Telemetry
